question: Using Huygens principle, show that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection for a plane wavefront reflected from a plane surface. Also mention the physical reason why the incident and reflected wavefronts travel with the same speed.

options.A: For a plane wavefront reflecting from a plane surface, each point reached at the surface emits secondary wavelets. Since the incident and reflected wavefronts are both in the same medium, they travel with the same speed $v$; in equal time both cover equal distances $vt$. The Huygens geometrical construction therefore gives equal angles with the normal: $i=r$.
options.B: Reflection changes medium, so the incident and reflected waves have different speeds. Hence $i\ne r$.
options.C: The reflected wavefront travels at zero speed at the reflecting surface, so its angle is always $90^\circ$.
options.D: Huygens construction gives $i+r=90^\circ$ because reflected wavelets travel in vacuum.
